content_voiceover: This is the sister trial to VIALE-A, called VIALE-C, and it tests venetoclax paired with low-dose cytarabine instead of azacitidine, again in unfit, newly diagnosed AML patients. Two hundred eleven patients, median age seventy-six, randomized two to one to venetoclax six hundred milligrams plus LDAC, or placebo plus LDAC. Look carefully at the two Kaplan-Meier panels, they show the same trial at two different analysis timepoints. At the primary endpoint analysis, the hazard ratio was zero point seven five but did not reach statistical significance, p equals zero point one one. However, with six more months of follow-up, the benefit became significant, hazard ratio zero point seven zero, p equals zero point zero four. Response rate was clearly better with venetoclax, forty-eight percent versus thirteen percent, and transfusion independence improved too, thirty-seven percent versus sixteen percent. The key teaching point here is that venetoclax plus LDAC is a reasonable option but generally considered less preferred than venetoclax plus azacitidine, partly because the survival benefit was borderline at the primary analysis and only became significant later.
keypoints: VIALE-C, venetoclax plus low-dose cytarabine in unfit AML, two hundred eleven patients
Primary endpoint hazard ratio zero point seven five, not significant, p equals zero point one one
With extended follow-up, hazard ratio zero point seven zero, p equals zero point zero four
Response rate forty-eight percent versus thirteen percent favoring venetoclax
Considered a less robust option than venetoclax plus azacitidine from VIALE-A
keypoint_voiceover: VIALE-C pairs venetoclax with low-dose cytarabine rather than azacitidine. The survival benefit only became statistically significant after extended follow-up, which is why most clinicians favor the azacitidine combination from VIALE-A as first choice.
